title: The Two Faces of What You Are
reflection: Once today, notice that you are aware without having switched anything on. Then notice that the awareness knows itself as present. Two faces, one flame.

questions.q: What does Prakāśa mean in Conversation 1.3?
o: The shining of awareness: it reveals, and you never have to switch the light on.
The stillness of awareness: it does not move, and it stays the same through all things.
The memory of awareness: it keeps a record of what has been seen in the past.
The effort of awareness: it works hard to bring each new thing into the light of day.
questions.e: Awareness is not a blank. It shines, revealing everything that appears, and no one ever switches that light on. Prakāśa is the revealing face.
questions.c: Prakāśa is the shining, revealing face

questions.q: What does Vimarśa add to Prakāśa, according to Conversation 1.3?
o: Self-presence: awareness is alive and knows itself as present, not only a light.
A second light: a weaker glow that appears only in the dark, where the first light fails.
A switch: the means by which a person turns the light of awareness on and off at will.
A screen: the blank surface on which the light of awareness falls and shows its images.
questions.e: A mirror reveals and a camera records, but neither knows it does. Awareness is alive: it knows itself as present. Vimarśa is that living, self-knowing face.
questions.c: Vimarśa is awareness knowing itself as present

questions.q: “Awareness is a blank screen: it shows everything and is nothing in itself.”
questions.e: It is not a blank screen. Awareness shines and it is alive. A mirror or a camera reveals or records without knowing it does; awareness reveals and knows itself as present.
questions.c: Awareness is not a blank screen

questions.q: A man thinks that a camera and awareness are the same thing, since each shows what is in front of it. What does Conversation 1.3 say?
o: The camera records but does not know that it does; awareness reveals and knows itself as present.
The camera is the better of the two, since it records everything exactly as it happened.
Awareness is the lesser of the two, since it forgets much of what it has once been shown.
They are the same, since a record and a knowing are one thing seen from two sides.
questions.e: A mirror or camera is light without self-presence: a machine. Awareness has both faces, shining and self-knowing, which is why it is not a mere recorder.
questions.c: A camera records; awareness also knows it is present

questions.q: “Light without self-presence is a machine, and self-presence without light is a blank point.”
questions.e: The two faces cannot be separated, like the brightness and the warmth of one flame. Take away either and you do not have awareness.
questions.c: The two faces cannot be separated

questions.q: What single name does the course use for the two faces together?
o: Consciousness-Energy: Consciousness for Prakāśa, and Energy, Śakti, for Vimarśa.
Mind-Matter: Mind for the shining, and Matter for the living, self-knowing face.
Body-Soul: Body for what appears, and Soul for what is aware of its appearing.
Thought-Feeling: Thought for the light, and Feeling for the knowing of the light.
questions.e: Consciousness is Prakāśa, the light that reveals; Energy is Vimarśa, Śakti, the living power that knows itself. One reality, two faces, with one name.
questions.c: Consciousness-Energy names the two faces together

questions.q: A woman reads that hearing a melody stirs the movement regions of the brain. Which idea of Conversation 1.3 does this support?
o: Embodied cognition: knowing is not a cold record but a living, bodily act, in line with Vimarśa.
Disembodied cognition: knowing happens apart from the body, in line with a blank screen.
Pure chance: the brain stirs for no reason, which has no bearing on how a person knows.
Forgetting: the brain drops one task to take up another, which is what a melody does.
questions.e: Hearing a melody stirs movement regions; reading the word sandpaper stirs the touch region. Knowing is alive and bodily, which echoes the living face of awareness.
questions.c: Embodied cognition echoes the living face

questions.q: A man is sure that his anxious habit is a verdict on who he is. What does Conversation 1.3 offer him?
o: The habit is a groove worn by use, not a verdict, and the same living power can wear a new one.
The habit is part of his nature, so he should learn to accept that he will always have it.
The habit is a mistake of the brain, so he should wait for a doctor to correct the fault.
The habit is imagined, so he should just decide that he does not have it and move on.
questions.e: Neuroplasticity shows that the brain rewires with use. Painful patterns are grooves worn by repeated use, and the same living power that wore them can wear new ones.

questions.q: A teacher wants to try the practical experiment of Conversation 1.3. What does she do?
o: Notice that she is aware without switching it on, and that it knows itself as present.
Switch her attention off for the day, so as to find out what is left when it is not on.
Count how many things she is aware of in an hour, and write the number down at night.
Compare her awareness with another person’s, to find out whose awareness is the brighter.
questions.e: The experiment is simple and direct: notice the light you never switch on, and the self-presence that comes with it. These are the two faces, seen at once.
questions.c: Notice the light and the self-presence together

questions.q: A woman is told that “awareness is only a state of the brain.” Which point of Conversation 1.3 helps her think about it?
o: Brain science matters, but the lesson sees awareness as shining and alive, not blank.
Brain activity is of no interest, so she should dismiss the claim without looking at any evidence.
Brain activity is the whole story, so she should accept the claim and drop the lesson at once.
Brain activity cannot be measured, so the claim is empty and there is nothing to think over.
questions.e: The lesson uses embodied cognition and neuroplasticity as friendly convergences, not as proofs, and keeps the two faces as what is seen by looking.
questions.c: Science converges but does not replace looking
